title: Communication and nonverbal
opens_on: CPQ-SF demand-withdraw or ACQ communication items.

specifics.text: Your partner's face looks angry and you don't know if they are. What do you do? What should they do?
Your partner has been quiet for two days. What do you assume, and what do you do?
Write-in: When my face looks upset, what's usually going on is ____.

preference.text: When you're upset, how do you want to be approached, in words you'd actually use?
Describe what good would look like here, concretely, in your house, on an ordinary week.

common.preference_universal: Describe what good would look like here, concretely, in your house, on an ordinary week.
common.tag_question: Is this a requirement, meaning the relationship doesn't work for you without it, or a preference, meaning you'd like it and could live without it?
common.tag_comment_prompt: In a sentence: what it means to you, and what it would look like met.
common.perception_gap: You rated yourself {self_value} on this and your partner rated you {partner_value}. What are you each seeing?
common.context: You flagged this one. What's the context?
common.polarization: You said that left to yourself you're at {self_alone} on this, and with your partner you find yourself at {self_with_partner}. What do you think is going on?
common.concreteness_followup: Can you give me a specific example?

transitions.enter: This topic came up. A few questions in your own words, one at a time. You can pause and come back any time.
transitions.consistency: A few follow-ups, written from your own answers. Each says why it is being asked, and skipping is fine.
transitions.complete: That's this topic done. Nothing here is shared until your partner has finished too.
